passages.text: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord and teacher of His disciples.
One day, Jesus prayed in a certain place.
After Jesus finished praying, one disciple spoke to Him.
The disciple said, “Lord, teach us to pray.”
John taught his disciples to pray.
The disciple wanted Jesus to teach them to pray in the same way.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον ὡς ἐπαύσατο εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν Κύριε δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them how to pray.
He said, “When you pray, say this.
Father, let Your name be holy.
Let Your kingdom come.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ὅταν προσεύχησθε λέγετε Πάτερ ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου Ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου

passages.text: Give us each day our daily bread.
passages.sermon: Jesus taught His disciples how to pray.\r\nHe told them to ask God for what they need each day.\r\nHe said, “Give us each day our daily bread.”
passages.original: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν

passages.text: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught his disciples how to pray.
He said, “Forgive us our sins.
We forgive everyone who sins against us.
Do not lead us into temptation.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν Καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν Καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread, because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He gave them an example.
He said, "Suppose you have a friend.
You go to your friend at midnight.
You say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves of bread.'
You explain, 'A friend of mine has come to me from a journey.'
You say, 'I have nothing to give him.'"
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ Φίλε χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ

passages.text: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
passages.sermon:
A man is inside his house.
Someone knocks on his door at midnight.
The man inside answers.
He says, “Do not bother me.”
He says, “My door is already shut.”
He says, “My children are with me in bed.”
He says, “I cannot get up to give you anything.”
passages.original: Κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι

passages.text: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them a story about a man and his friend.
The man needed bread at midnight.
He went to his friend’s house and asked for three loaves.
The friend did not want to get up.
He did not want to help, even though they were friends.
He said the door was shut.
He said his children were in bed with him.
He said he could not get up to give anything.
Jesus said the friend would not get up just because they were friends.
But the man kept asking.
He was persistent.
Because of this persistence, the friend got up.
He gave the man as much as he needed.
passages.original: Λέγω ὑμῖν εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει

passages.text: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He gives them clear instructions.
He says, "Ask God for what you need.
God will give it to you.
Seek what you are looking for.
You will find it.
Knock at the door.
God will open the door for you."
passages.original: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω αἰτεῖτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν ζητεῖτε καὶ εὑρήσετε κρούετε καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
passages.sermon: Everyone who asks receives.\r\nEveryone who seeks finds.\r\nGod opens the door to everyone who knocks.
passages.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται

passages.text: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
passages.sermon: A father loves his child.\r\nA son may ask his father for a fish.\r\nNo father among you would give his son a snake instead of a fish.
passages.original: Τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει

passages.text: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
passages.sermon:
A father cares for his child.
A son may ask his father for an egg.
The father will not give his son a scorpion instead.
A good father gives good things to his child.
He does not give something harmful when his child asks for something good.
passages.original: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον

passages.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said that they are sinful.
He said that even though they are sinful, they know how to give good gifts to their children.
God is the Father in heaven.
God is not sinful.
God is good.
God gives even better gifts than people do.
God gives the Holy Spirit.
God gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed, but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was driving out a demon.
This demon had made a man mute.
When Jesus cast out the demon, the mute man spoke.
The crowds saw this and were amazed.
Some people in the crowd spoke.
They said, “He drives out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν κωφόν ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.
passages.sermon: Some people wanted to test Jesus.\r\nThey asked Jesus for a sign from heaven.
passages.original: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew what they were thinking.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Every kingdom that is divided against itself will be destroyed.
A house that is divided against itself will fall.”
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει

passages.text: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew the thoughts of the people.
Jesus spoke to them.
Satan is an evil spiritual being.
Satan has a kingdom.
If Satan is divided against himself, his kingdom cannot stand.
You say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
Beelzebul is another name for a powerful evil spirit.
You accuse me of using Beelzebul’s power to cast out demons.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people who accused him of using Beelzebul’s power.
He said, “If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, then think about your own sons.”
Your sons also drive out demons.
By whose power do they do this?
Your own sons will judge you.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται

passages.text: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus has power over demons.
Jesus drives out demons by the finger of God.
The finger of God means God's own power.
If Jesus drives out demons by God's power, something important has happened.
The kingdom of God has come upon the people.
God's rule is now present among them.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ Θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.
passages.sermon:
A strong man stands guard over his own house.
He wears full armor.
He protects his house.
His possessions remain safe.
No one disturbs his peace.
passages.original: Ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.
passages.sermon:
A stronger person comes.
This stronger person attacks the first man.
The stronger person defeats the first man.
The first man trusted in his armor.
The stronger person takes away the first man’s armor.
The stronger person divides the first man’s possessions.
passages.original: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν

passages.text: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus claims authority and power.
Anyone who is not with Jesus stands against Jesus.
Anyone who does not gather with Jesus scatters.
passages.original: Ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει

passages.text: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’
passages.sermon:
An unclean spirit can live inside a person.
When the unclean spirit leaves the person, it goes away.
The unclean spirit travels through dry places.
It looks for a place to rest.
It does not find any rest.
Then the unclean spirit says, “I will return to my house, the place I left.”
passages.original: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν καὶ μὴ εὑρίσκον τότε λέγει Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον

passages.text: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
passages.sermon: The unclean spirit returns to the man.\r\nIt finds the man’s life clean.\r\nIt finds the man’s life put in order.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον

passages.text: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”
passages.sermon:
The unclean spirit leaves a man.
It goes and finds seven other spirits.
These seven spirits are more wicked than itself.
The unclean spirit brings these seven spirits with it.
They all enter the man.
They live there together.
The man’s final condition becomes worse than before.
passages.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων

passages.text: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking to the people.
A woman stood in the crowd.
She raised her voice.
She spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Blessed is the womb that carried You.
Blessed are the breasts that nursed You.”
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας

passages.text: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
He answered the woman who praised His mother.
He said, “Blessed are those who hear the word of God.
Blessed are those who obey the word of God.”
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες

passages.text: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the crowds growing larger.
Jesus began to speak.
Jesus said, “This generation is wicked.
This generation asks for a sign.
No sign will be given to this generation.
The only sign will be the sign of Jonah.”
passages.original: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν σημεῖον ζητεῖ καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ

passages.text: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds.
He called their generation wicked.
He said the people wanted a sign.
He told them they would not receive a sign except the sign of Jonah.
Jonah was a sign to the people of Nineveh.
In the same way, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
passages.original: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο Ἰωνᾶς τοῖς Νινευίταις σημεῖον οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ

passages.text: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
passages.sermon:
The Queen of the South is a woman who lived far away.
She traveled a great distance to meet King Solomon.
She wanted to hear Solomon’s wisdom.
At the time of judgment, the Queen of the South will stand up.
She will stand with the men of this generation.
She will condemn this generation.
She will do this because she valued wisdom and came from far away to hear it.
Now someone greater than Solomon is here.
This generation does not listen to him.
The Queen of the South will show that this generation is wrong.
passages.original: Βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε

passages.text: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
passages.sermon:
The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation.
They will condemn this generation.
The men of Nineveh repented when Jonah preached to them.
Now someone greater than Jonah is here.
passages.original: ἄνδρες Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε

passages.text: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
passages.sermon:
No one lights a lamp and hides it in a cellar.
No one puts a lamp under a basket.
A person puts a lamp on a stand.
He does this so people who enter can see the light.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φέγγος βλέπωσιν

passages.text: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
passages.sermon:
Your eye is the lamp of your body.
Your eye lets light into your body.
When your eyes are good, your whole body is full of light.
When your eyes are bad, your body is full of darkness.
passages.original: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν

passages.text: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He taught them about light and darkness inside a person.
He said, “Be careful.”
Make sure the light inside you is not darkness.
Examine yourself.
Do not let what should be light become darkness within you.
passages.original: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν

passages.text: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His listeners.
He explained the importance of spiritual light.
He said, “If your whole body is full of light,
and if no part of your body is in darkness,
then your whole body will be full of light.
You will shine brightly.
You will be radiant, like a lamp shining its light on you.”
passages.original: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν μὴ ἔχον μέρος τι σκοτεινόν ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε

passages.text: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking.
A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him.
Jesus went into the Pharisee’s house.
Jesus sat down at the table.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν

passages.text: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
passages.sermon:
A Pharisee watched Jesus.
The Pharisee felt surprised.
Jesus did not wash before the meal.
The Pharisee noticed this.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου

passages.text: “Now then,” said the Lord, “you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisee.
Jesus addressed the Pharisees directly.
Jesus said, “You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup.
You also clean the outside of the dish.
But inside, you are full of greed.
Inside, you are full of wickedness.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας

passages.text: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He called them fools.
God made the outside of a person.
God also made the inside of a person.
God created both the outward and inward parts.
passages.original: ἄφρονες οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν

passages.text: But give as alms the things that are within you, and you will see that everything is clean for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He told them to give what is inside them as alms.
He meant they should give from their hearts.
He meant they should show mercy and generosity from within.
If they do this, everything will be clean for them.
passages.original: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν

passages.text: Woe to you Pharisees! You pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
Jesus said, “Woe to you, Pharisees!”
You give a tenth of your mint.
You give a tenth of your rue.
You give a tenth of every herb.
But you neglect justice.
You neglect the love of God.
You should have done justice.
You should have loved God.
You should not have neglected giving tithes.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι

passages.text: Woe to you Pharisees! You love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees are religious leaders.
They love to sit in the best seats in the synagogues.
They love to receive greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you Pharisees!
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς

passages.text: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He warned them.
He said, “Woe to you!”
You are like unmarked graves.
People walk over these graves.
They do not know what is beneath them.
People do not notice the graves.
People do not realize what they are walking on.
passages.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν

passages.text: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”
passages.sermon: An expert in the law spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said, “Teacher, you insult us when you say these things.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις

passages.text: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “You weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law.
He said, "Woe to you as well."
You are experts in the law.
You place heavy burdens on people.
These burdens are hard to carry.
You do not help people with these burdens.
You will not lift even one finger to lighten their load.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις

passages.text: Woe to you! You build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law.
He said, “Woe to you!”
You build tombs for the prophets.
Your fathers killed those prophets.
passages.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς

passages.text: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law.
You are witnesses to what your fathers did.
You agree with your fathers’ actions.
Your fathers killed the prophets.
You build the tombs for those prophets.
passages.original: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε

passages.text: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
passages.sermon:
God is wise.
God spoke with wisdom.
God said, “I will send prophets to these people.
I will also send apostles to them.
Some of these prophets and apostles they will kill.
They will persecute others of them.”
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ Θεοῦ εἶπεν Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ διώξουσιν

passages.text: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of His time.
He said this generation will be held responsible.
They will be charged with the blood of all the prophets.
This blood has been shed since the foundation of the world.
It includes the blood of Abel.
It includes the blood of Zechariah.
Zechariah was killed between the altar and the sanctuary.
Yes, Jesus said, all of this will be charged to this generation.
passages.original: ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου ναί λέγω ὑμῖν ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης

passages.text: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law.
He said, "Woe to you."
You have taken away the key to knowledge.
You did not enter yourselves.
You stopped others who were trying to enter.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε

passages.text: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things, waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left that place.
The scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Jesus strongly.
They asked Jesus many questions.
They tried to trap Jesus with His own words.
They waited to catch Jesus saying something wrong.
passages.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων ἐνεδρεύοντες αὐτὸν θηρεῦσαί τι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ
